body:
Found at sign-off of #531 (PR #637), recorded in that bundle's §10 and the PR's "Known limits". Not fixed there.

**What happens.** In merge mode, `_fetch` (`template/src/pdca_harness/merge.py:256-259` on `fix/531-merge-mode-stale-base-merge`) fetches only `cfg.base_remote` and `origin`. A stacked publish pushes the PR branch to the brief's `Onto branch` remote (`publish.py`, `git push <remote> HEAD:<branch>`), and that can be a third remote. After `gh pr update-branch`, the new merge commit exists only on that remote. `_contains` then gets git exit 128 ("not a valid commit"), and the run refuses with "git failed".

**Effect.** Fail-closed, so nothing merges wrongly. But a PR on a third remote can never merge in merge mode once it falls behind, and the message doesn't name the real cause.

**Fix, one of:**
- fetch the remote named in the bundle's publish record as well, or
- when the head commit isn't in the checkout, say exactly that instead of "git failed".

If `Onto branch` can't happen in merge mode, refuse that combination up front and close this issue.

Source: `results/issue_531/SUMMARY.md` §10 and `pr-description.md` "Known limits" (pdca-pdca).
title: merge mode: a PR pushed to a third remote can never merge once behind — _fetch reads only base_remote and origin, and the refusal says "git failed"
